subject.title: Feature: Silence Watchdog + Response Delivery Confirmation — runtime-enforced operator visibility

question: Should OpenClaw keep this as a single combined core feature, or route the work through the narrower watchdog, durable final-delivery, and delivery-failure notification contracts already open?
rationale: The proposal changes default operator-visible behavior, delivery retry/alert semantics, duplicate suppression, and per-channel configuration across gateway/channel runtime paths, which code inspection cannot safely choose without maintainer product intent.

options.title: Route Through Narrower Contracts
options.body: Keep this issue open as umbrella context while maintainers sequence implementation through the existing watchdog, durable final-delivery, and delivery-status issues.

options.title: Sponsor Combined Feature
options.body: Approve one broad core feature and require explicit defaults, config migration posture, duplicate-suppression semantics, and live-channel proof before implementation.

options.title: Defer New Defaults
options.body: Continue relying on heartbeat, pending-final, and delivery queue foundations until stronger live evidence justifies new default channel-visible behavior.

recommendation.title: Route Through Narrower Contracts
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as umbrella context while maintainers sequence implementation through the existing watchdog, durable final-delivery, and delivery-status issues.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for the central pending-final, outbound delivery, and durable queue seams points to steipete.
